destination.title: Vacuum construction and control
destination.question: Which vacua and stabilization mechanisms exist in specified compactifications or effective theories, and when do they survive backreaction, localization and corrections?
destination.summary: Separate constructing stationary solutions from establishing stability, approximation control and a string realization.

regimes: Source-specific classical, perturbative, asymptotic and quantum-corrected settings
assumptions: A controlled effective-theory parameter does not by itself establish control of omitted string corrections.
conventions: Flat directions, metastability and complete stabilization are distinct outcomes.
excludes: A universal controlled de Sitter construction

sources.title: Smeared versus localised sources in flux compactifications

evidence.text: When do flux vacua constructed using smeared orientifolds or D-branes survive source localisation, and how does the answer depend on BPS relations and the resulting warping, dilaton and RR-field corrections?

sources.title: Charting the landscape of N=4 flux compactifications

evidence.text: Which SO(3)-invariant vacua occur in isotropic Z2×Z2 flux compactifications with one set of sources, and which remain stable after including the full N=4 scalar spectrum?

sources.title: On the Flux Vacua in F-theory Compactifications

evidence.text: Can mirror-symmetry data including brane deformations produce F-theory flux vacua that stabilize all complex-structure fields near a large-complex-structure point?

sources.title: Flux vacua with approximate flat directions

evidence.text: Can quantized flux choices produce type IIB vacua with approximate flat directions beyond constructions requiring a homogeneous quadratic superpotential, providing new starting points for small W0 and phenomenology?

sources.title: Analytics of type IIB flux vacua and their mass spectra

evidence.text: Which type IIB flux configurations allow analytic axio-dilaton/complex-structure vacuum locations and mass spectra for arbitrarily many fields, and how do quadratic superpotentials and polynomial large-complex-structure corrections govern stabilization and flat directions?

sources.title: Effective potentials, warping, and implications for F-term uplifting

evidence.text: How does non-ISD flux backreaction modify the off-shell Type IIB flux potential, and can complex-structure F-term uplifting remain controlled after warping and quantum corrections?

sources.title: Moduli stabilization from magnetic fluxes in type I string theory

evidence.text: Can quantized, constant open-string magnetic backgrounds stabilize Kähler and complex-structure moduli in four-dimensional supersymmetric type I vacua, with an exact string description and tunably large internal dimensions?

sources.title: Fixing moduli in exact type IIA flux vacua

evidence.text: Do the supersymmetric type IIA flux vacua obtained from four-dimensional effective theory admit ten-dimensional descriptions, how does flux/O6 backreaction modify Calabi–Yau geometry, and how does ten-dimensional flux quantization fix moduli?

sources.title: Smeared versus localised sources in flux compactifications

evidence.text: Construct localised solutions by adding a warp factor, a sourced RR component and a varying dilaton. The remaining equations reduce to relations among these fields and a Poisson equation with flux and delta-function source terms.

sources.title: Charting the landscape of N=4 flux compactifications

evidence.text: Combine extremization equations with embedding-tensor quadratic constraints into an ideal; use Singular and the Gianni–Trager–Zacharias primary-decomposition algorithm, then solve simpler factors analytically and retain real flux solutions.

sources.title: On the Flux Vacua in F-theory Compactifications

evidence.text: Use fourfold periods of the holomorphic (4,0)-form and a moduli-independent intersection pairing to construct the complex-structure Kähler potential and flux superpotential. Both the cycle basis and chosen G4 fluxes are restricted to primary horizontal cohomology.

sources.title: Flux vacua with approximate flat directions

evidence.text: Use polynomial equations from the perturbative prepotential, explicit factorization and duality transformations. For toroidal isolation tests, linearize all 11 equations in the 10 variables (τij,φ): rank deficiency is necessary for a continuous family, including possible off-diagonal deformations.

sources.title: Analytics of type IIB flux vacua and their mass spectra

evidence.text: The quadratic vacuum equations are separated into axionic and saxionic systems after showing W is real on shell. Matrix image/kernel conditions and the generalized inverse M⁺ organize flux constraints, flat directions and Q′ = Q − ½LᵀM⁺L.

sources.title: Effective potentials, warping, and implications for F-term uplifting

evidence.text: Use harmonic-form expansions and special geometry to match zero-mode obstructions to derivatives of the leading four-dimensional potential. Estimate stability through Hessian projections and induced vacuum shifts. The calculation targets the potential; compensator-dependent kinetic terms are not derived.

sources.title: Moduli stabilization in asymptotic flux compactifications

evidence.text: How can flux vacua be studied systematically near different boundaries of complex-structure moduli space, rather than by solving a separate transcendental problem for every compactification?

sources.title: Asymptotic Flux Compactifications and the Swampland

evidence.text: Do restrictions on flux vacua and axion dynamics survive beyond weak coupling and large volume? The paper approaches this question through four-form flux potentials near boundaries of Calabi–Yau complex-structure moduli space, including boundaries at finite distance.

sources.title: An index for flux vacua

evidence.text: Can boundary or asymptotic information about a scalar potential establish the existence of interior critical points, and can an index of DW establish supersymmetric flux vacua?

sources.title: Flux compactification

evidence.text: How can flux compactification stabilize moduli and produce long-lived candidate vacua with broken supersymmetry and small positive cosmological constant, and what can their abundance and distribution imply for observable physics?

sources.title: Connecting flux vacua through scalar field excursions

evidence.text: Can flux vacua with different integer fluxes become critical points of one scalar potential after integrating in open-string fields, permitting scalar-metric distances and tests of exponential tower-mass decay?

sources.title: D-brane Deconstructions in IIB Orientifolds

evidence.text: How can one systematically compute globally consistent D7-brane charges, deformation moduli, flux lattices, gauge groups and matter, and construct worldvolume-flux vacua when generic orientifold D7 worldvolumes are singular?

sources.title: Moduli potentials in string compactifications with fluxes: Mapping the discretuum

evidence.text: Can flux compactifications stabilize all moduli through F-terms while producing broken supersymmetry, a small nonnegative cosmological constant, and a hierarchy within weak coupling and large volume? Are the resulting vacua cosmologically viable?

sources.title: Physics of String Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: How do fluxes stabilize compactification moduli and generate large vacuum ensembles, and what can statistical analysis of those ensembles say about cosmological constants, supersymmetry breaking, and the testability of string theory?

sources.title: Obstacles to Constructing de Sitter Space in String Theory

evidence.text: When does a candidate flux vacuum belong to a controllable approximation? The paper requires a family of discrete flux choices along which the relevant expansion parameters become small, rather than favorable values at one isolated stationary point.

sources.title: Supersymmetry breaking and alpha-prime corrections to flux induced potentials

evidence.text: Which flux-induced M-theory vacua break supersymmetry while retaining zero three-dimensional cosmological constant and leading-order stability, and do perturbative α′ corrections destroy the corresponding no-scale structure in Type IIB compactifications?

sources.title: Some Physical Consequences of an Exact Vacua Distribution in the Bousso-Polchinski Landscape

evidence.text: How can lattice vacua in very thin cosmological-constant shells be counted beyond the Bousso–Polchinski volume approximation, and what does the resulting distribution imply for flux occupation, the smallest positive cosmological constant and possible moduli-stabilization difficulties?

sources.title: Generalized Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Which supersymmetric vacua arise in the generalized-flux four-dimensional theory, can their coupling and cosmological constant be tuned, and does their apparent accumulation challenge landscape finiteness?

sources.title: Flux compactifications in string theory: A Comprehensive review

evidence.text: How do closed-string fluxes support four-dimensional type II vacua, constrain internal geometry, generate effective potentials and stabilize moduli? The review also examines corrections, proposed de Sitter constructions and statistical distributions of vacua.

sources.title: TASI / PiTP / ISS lectures on moduli and microphysics

evidence.text: How do string-theoretic forces stabilize moduli and produce cosmological vacua, what microphysical degrees of freedom account for their entropy, and how do velocity-dependent effects change moduli dynamics?

sources.title: Distributions of nonsupersymmetric flux vacua

evidence.text: What determines the density and supersymmetry-breaking scale distribution of metastable nonsupersymmetric vacua in supergravity ensembles, especially Type IIB flux compactifications, and how do near-zero vacuum energy and additional D-type contributions change the result?

sources.title: Massive IIA flux compactifications and U-dualities

evidence.text: Do the DeWolfe et al. massive IIA orientifold vacua admit systematic large-flux low-energy or weak-string-coupling expansions once orientifold backreaction is included, and can dual descriptions clarify their dimensionality?

sources.title: Type IIA Flux Vacua with Mobile D6-branes

evidence.text: Can classical type IIA flux vacua retain a positive semidefinite potential and non-supersymmetric Minkowski minima when mobile D6-branes mix open and closed moduli, and what supersymmetry-breaking and soft-term patterns follow?

sources.title: Seeing through the String Landscape - a String Hunter's Companion in Particle Physics and Cosmology

evidence.text: How can top-down consistency, bottom-up Standard Model construction, landscape statistics and particle/cosmological signatures make classes of string vacua predictive? This is a review spanning intersecting branes, flux stabilization, domain walls and inflation.

sources.title: Testing Swampland Conjectures with Machine Learning

evidence.text: Can discrete flux patterns explain small vacuum energy within a perturbative compactification and organize spectra compatible with proposed quantum-gravity restrictions?

sources.title: Chaotic coupling constants

evidence.text: Can finite-volume string moduli spaces and chaotic early-universe motion reduce initial-condition tuning in vacuum selection, and can conjectural S-duality constrain the nonperturbative potentials responsible for dilaton stabilization and supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: Lectures on constructing string vacua

evidence.text: How can approximate, controlled string vacua suitable for phenomenological model building be constructed and analyzed, especially IIB/F-theory flux compactifications with stabilized moduli, and what obstructs control?

sources.title: Asymptotic Hodge Theory in String Compactifications and Integrable Systems

evidence.text: How can asymptotic Hodge theory characterize couplings and flux-vacuum loci in type IIB/F-theory compactifications, and construct solutions of certain two-dimensional integrable sigma models?

sources.title: Low energy supersymmetry from R-symmetries

evidence.text: When does a continuous or discrete R-symmetry provide a sufficient condition for a supersymmetric vacuum with W = 0, allowing arbitrary field R-charges, and how can this condition be realized in Type IIB flux compactifications?

sources.title: Exponentially Small Cosmological Constant in String Theory

evidence.text: Can quantized data in a string compactification generate vacuum energy below 10^−123 M_pl^4 and extreme separation between the compactification radius and spacetime curvature radius, without an exhaustive search through exponentially many flux choices?

sources.title: Moduli Stabilization in String Theory

evidence.text: How can string compactifications yield isolated four-dimensional vacua with massive moduli and broken supersymmetry, while retaining computational control and supporting realistic cosmology and particle physics?

sources.title: Asymmetric CFTs and GSUGRA

evidence.text: Do certain asymmetric conformal field theories describe the same vacua as fully backreacted gauged supergravities, thereby providing string realizations of non-geometric gaugings and partial supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: A gravitino distance conjecture

evidence.text: Which asymptotic type IIA vacuum families can be studied using a fixed two-modulus growth sector while retaining large volume and weak coupling?

sources.title: Models of Particle Physics from Type IIB String Theory and F-theory: A Review

evidence.text: Which tools and constructions in type IIB string theory and F-theory can combine moduli stabilization, supersymmetry breaking, chiral matter and realistic interactions into particle-physics vacua?

sources.title: Progress in D-brane model building

evidence.text: How can D-branes produce weakly coupled four-dimensional N=1 type II orientifold vacua with semi-realistic gauge sectors, and how do background fluxes change the allowed branes, effective couplings, moduli stabilization and supersymmetry breaking?

destination.title: Distributions, tuning and predictivity
destination.question: How do specified vacuum ensembles distribute low-energy quantities, and what conditional conclusions about tuning, typicality and predictivity follow?
destination.summary: Ensemble distributions, coupling scans and observational conditioning require separate assumptions.

systems: Supergravity and interacting chiral-field landscape models
assumptions: Sampling, coupling probability laws and population measures are not interchangeable.
An effective landscape model is not automatically a realized string ensemble.
conventions: Selection-conditioned distributions remain distinguished from unconditioned counts.
includes: Comparisons of analytic and explicit distributions

sources.title: TASI Lectures on the Cosmological Constant

evidence.text: Approximate a thin energy shell by its continuum volume and compare that volume with a lattice cell. The operation estimates configuration abundance, with arithmetic and degeneracy checks needed for claims about actual nearby energy levels.

sources.title: Applications of an exact counting formula in the Bousso-Polchinski Landscape

evidence.text: Steepest descent and numerical saddle solutions approximate the exact integral. Inclusion–exclusion counts states with exactly j occupied flux directions; numerical sampling and brute-force searches support selected approximations. Thin-shell counts use Nε≈ω_J(R0)Λε/R0.

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: Solve section-degree constraints without denominator coordinates, extract minimal divisor factors, and identify the candidate fiber. Check monodromy and matter separately before concluding non-Higgsability.

sources.title: Testing Swampland Conjectures with Machine Learning

evidence.text: Construct polynomial functions, apply their sign-kernel transforms, and combine them in a finite antisymmetrized sum. This operation needs convergent weights and consistent polynomial and variance conventions. The displayed version fails the convergence requirement, independently of the unread cited sources.

sources.title: The Statistics of string / M theory vacua

evidence.text: Uses Witten-index/Euler-characteristic and top-Chern-class estimates, Gaussian random-superpotential integrals, and smoothing of quantized-flux delta sums to construct tractable ensemble approximations.

sources.title: Distributions of nonsupersymmetric flux vacua

evidence.text: Counts critical points using an ensemble integral with δ(V′)|det V″|, imposing Hessian positivity for metastability. The determinant is the Jacobian giving unit weight per isolated vacuum, physically involving the product of bosonic squared masses.
